correctness.rationale: All definitions, quantifiers and boundary \(n\ge16\) for the explicit bound are controlled. For nonzero displacement a, the domain-to-image edges form a forest, giving \(2^{n-r}\) commuting idempotents and the exact mixed count. For two nonzero displacements, each of \(n-4h\) interior commutation constraints equates two independent Bernoulli products with equality probability \(5/8\); their dependency graph has degree at most four, yielding an independent subset of at least \((n-4h)/5\). Large displacements are suppressed by a geometric count. These imply the stated exponential bound and conditional-idempotent limit. Literal composition checks through \(n=9\) reproduced all finite-size formulas; these finite checks are corroboration only.

value.rationale: Commutation probability is a canonical invariant of finite inverse monoids. Exact rank-resolved centralizers of the Boolean idempotent semilattice and exponential suppression of every other commuting contribution give a structural probabilistic theorem not implied by the known monoid cardinality. The one-ninth limit contrasts with the three-tenths interval-submonoid law and explains why the limit is carried entirely by idempotents. The theorem treats an infinite natural family and requires a nontrivial dependent-event bound.
